one_liner: Senior contracting officer at DOJ's Office of Acquisition Management who plans, awards, negotiates, and administers complex, high-dollar federal contracts.
fit_summary: This GS-14 role needs at least 4 years of contracting experience, 1 year at the GS-13 equivalent, a FAC-C (Professional) certification or a documented path to one, and 24 semester hours in business-type fields. Daniel's IEM consulting background in emergency management and public policy is adjacent but not procurement work. Unless Daniel actually wrote RFPs, chose contract types, or handled modifications and closeouts for years, this posting is likely out of reach for now.
eligibility: Open to the public and through the federal transition path via Direct Hire Authority, so no federal status is required and veterans' preference does not apply.

Basic requirement: at least 4 years of contracting or related experience, including 1 year of specialized experience at the GS-13 level that meets 2 of the 4 listed statements (solicitations/RFPs, contract type selection, modifications/justifications/D&Fs, QA/disputes/closeout).

Education: a 4-year bachelor's degree with at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, industrial management, marketing, quantitative methods, or organization and management; transcripts must be uploaded.
You must hold, or be able to earn within 12 months of appointment, a FAC-C (Professional) or DAWIA contracting certification, and you must attach documentation.
You must pass the USA Hire online assessment and meet all requirements by the cut-off you apply under (initial cut-off 08/27/2026).
strategy: Check honestly whether your IEM work involved procurement tasks such as writing proposals responding to government RFPs, managing task orders, or tracking contract deliverables. Proposal-side work is related but rarely equals GS-13 contracting-officer experience.
Pull your transcript and count your semester hours in the 24-hour business-type fields. If you fall short, this role is closed to you regardless of experience.

If you lack the experience, target entry-level GS-1102 roles (GS-7/9, often called Acquisition Intern or Pathways Recent Graduate) or emergency-management and program-analyst roles at FEMA, Virginia VDEM, or Prince William County, where your IEM background fits directly.
If you do qualify, describe each specialized-experience statement in your own words with specific contract values and dates. HR will rate you ineligible if you copy the statement into your resume.
Keep the resume within two pages, listing hours per week, dates, and contract dollar values, and attach transcripts and FAC-C/DAWIA documentation before the 08/27/2026 initial cut-off.
Preview the questionnaire at the posted USA Staffing link and answer only at levels your resume clearly supports.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] [emergency management/disaster recovery] contracts valued at [$X] by [drafting proposal sections / tracking deliverables / preparing task order documentation], [hours per week], [dates].
Coordinated with [client contracting officer / program staff] on [number] [modifications / task orders / performance reports], ensuring compliance with [contract terms / FAR requirements].
Evaluated [vendor/subcontractor] performance against [statement of work requirements], resolving [type of issue] and documenting results for [client/closeout].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you selected a contract type for a complex services requirement and justified that choice.
Describe a contract dispute or performance problem you resolved and the steps you took.
How do you prepare a justification or determination and findings, and get it through approvals?
Tell us about a time you negotiated a modification with a contractor under time pressure.
watch_outs: The experience and FAC-C certification requirements are very likely unmet given Daniel's known background, so an application may be rated ineligible.
Transcripts with 24 business-related semester hours are mandatory, and a policy or political science degree alone may not count.
Applications received after the 08/27/2026 initial cut-off are considered only if more vacancies open.
The position is in Washington, DC with telework but not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas on in-office days.
